title: Triangle squares in coherent cone mapping simplicial sets
statement: Use small simplicial sets with the ordered join $\star$ of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone], small simplicial categories with subset-poset coherent realization $\mathfrak C$ of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], and marked simplicial sets of [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model]. Let $K$ be any small simplicial set, let $v$ be a new cone vertex, put $P=\mathfrak C[K\star\Delta^0]$ and $X_x=P(x,v)$ for each vertex $x$ of $K$. For an edge $e:x\to y$, write $e^*:X_y\to X_x$ for precomposition by its coherent-realization vertex and $\widetilde e:\widetilde x\to e^*\widetilde y$ for the edge induced by its coning triangle. Here $\widetilde x\in X_x$ is the cone arrow from $x$ to $v$. Give $X_x$ the marking $E_x$ consisting of all degenerate edges and all $g^*\widetilde d$ with $d$ a degenerate edge of $K$ and $g\in\mathfrak C[K](x,\operatorname{source}(d))_1$; the star means the diagonal simplicial precomposition action. For every $2$-simplex $\sigma$ of $K$ with edges $e:x\to y$, $f:y\to z$, $k:x\to z$, let $\rho_\sigma$ be the edge from $k$ to the coherent composite $fe$ in $\mathfrak C[K](x,z)$ obtained from $\{0,2\}\subseteq\{0,1,2\}$. There is a simplicial square $H_\sigma:\Delta^1\times\Delta^1\to X_x$ with vertices $\widetilde x,e^*\widetilde y,k^*\widetilde z,e^*f^*\widetilde z$ at $(0,0),(1,0),(0,1),(1,1)$ respectively, whose edges at the second coordinate $0$ and $1$ are $\widetilde e$ and $\rho_\sigma^*\widetilde z$, and whose edges at the first coordinate $0$ and $1$ are $\widetilde k$ and $e^*\widetilde f$. The edge $\rho_\sigma^*\widetilde z$ is marked in $E_x$. If $k$ is degenerate then $\widetilde k$ is marked as well. Precomposition by any vertex of $\mathfrak C[K](w,x)$ carries $E_x$ into $E_w$ and carries this square to a square with the corresponding four precomposed edges. These assertions hold for degenerate $\sigma$ as well and require neither $K$ nor its coherent mapping simplicial sets to be Kan.

proof.text:
Write $[1]=\{0<1\}$. By the subset-poset definition in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], an $m$-simplex of $\mathfrak C[\Delta^3](0,3)$ is a chain of subsets containing $0,3$. For an $m$-simplex $(a,b)$ of $\Delta^1\times\Delta^1$, that is, monotone maps $a,b:[m]\to[1]$, put
$$S_j=\{0,3\}\cup\{1:a(j)=1\}\cup\{2:b(j)=1\},\quad 0\leq j\leq m.$$
These subsets are increasing, and restriction along any monotone map replaces $S_j$ by the correspondingly indexed subset. This defines a simplicial map $q:\Delta^1\times\Delta^1\to\mathfrak C[\Delta^3](0,3)$. The ordered join of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone] with $\Delta^0$ appends a last vertex, so $\Delta^2\star\Delta^0=\Delta^3$, and $\sigma\star\mathrm{id}$ induces a simplicial functor $F:\mathfrak C[\Delta^3]\to P$ taking $0,1,2,3$ to $x,y,z,v$. Set $H_\sigma=F_{0,3}q$. No injectivity of $\sigma$ is used.

source.place: Section 1.1.5, subset-poset coherent realization; explicit cube underlying Proposition 3.2.1.11(4), printed p.175.

proof.text: The four vertices of $q$ are $\{0,3\},\{0,1,3\},\{0,2,3\},\{0,1,2,3\}$, in the order $(0,0),(1,0),(0,1),(1,1)$. Union composition in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] sends them under $F$ to $\widetilde x,e^*\widetilde y,k^*\widetilde z,e^*f^*\widetilde z$. On the bottom and left boundaries the subset chains are respectively $\{0,3\}\subseteq\{0,1,3\}$ and $\{0,3\}\subseteq\{0,2,3\}$: the coning triangles of $e$ and $k$ give precisely these chains. Thus their images are $\widetilde e,\widetilde k$. The right boundary is $\{0,1,3\}\subseteq\{0,1,2,3\}$, the union of the constant subset $\{0,1\}$ with $\{1,3\}\subseteq\{1,2,3\}$; its image is $e^*\widetilde f$. The top boundary is $\{0,2,3\}\subseteq\{0,1,2,3\}$, the union of $\{0,2\}\subseteq\{0,1,2\}$ with the constant subset $\{2,3\}$; its image is $\rho_\sigma^*\widetilde z$. These are equalities of edges, since the entire two-element chains, not just their endpoints, have been computed.

source.place: Notation 3.2.1.1 and the first displayed square in Proposition 3.2.1.11(4), printed pp.170-171 and 175; four boundary chains computed explicitly.

proof.text: For a vertex $t$ of $K$, the coning triangle $s_0t\star v=s_0(t\star v)$ (degeneracies of the join act on the initial block, [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]) factors through the cone edge by the monotone map $[2]\to[1]$ taking $0,1$ to $0$ and $2$ to $1$. Its direct-image map on subsets sends both $\{0,2\}$ and $\{0,1,2\}$ to $\{0,1\}$. (Direct image preserves unions and inclusions, which defines the induced coherent functor of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison].) Consequently $\widetilde{s_0t}=s_0\widetilde t$. Apply this with $t=z$. Diagonal composition of $\rho_\sigma$ with $s_0\widetilde z$ is exactly $\rho_\sigma^*\widetilde z$, so this top edge is the generator $g^*\widetilde d$ with $g=\rho_\sigma$ and $d=s_0z$ in the stipulated $E_x$. If $k$ is degenerate, then $k=s_0x$ and the same calculation makes $\widetilde k=s_0\widetilde x$, which belongs to $E_x$. These are marking memberships in the sense of [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model]; no closure under composition of marked edges is assumed.

source.place: Notation 3.2.1.1 and Definition 3.2.1.2, printed p.171; degenerate-edge and diagonal-action calculation.

proof.text:
For a vertex $a\in\mathfrak C[K](w,x)_0$, precomposition is the simplicial map $a^*:X_x\to X_w$ obtained by composing with the constant simplices on $a$. The associativity and simplicial composition of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] give, on an edge generator,
$$a^*(g^*\widetilde d)=(g\circ s_0a)^*\widetilde d.$$
Here $g\circ s_0a$ is an edge of $\mathfrak C[K](w,\operatorname{source}(d))$, so the right side is a generator of $E_w$. Degenerate edges map to degenerate edges because $a^*$ is simplicial. Thus $a^*$ preserves the markings. The composite $a^*H_\sigma$ is a simplicial square, and restricting it to each boundary gives exactly $a^*$ applied to the corresponding computed edge. This proves both precomposition assertions.

source.place: Definition 3.2.1.2 and Proposition 3.2.1.11(4), printed pp.171 and 175-176; fixed-vertex precomposition.

proof.text: The construction in Step 1 applies to every map $\Delta^2\to K$, including degenerate simplices: it uses the functor induced by that map and never a lifting or an embedding. All boundary equalities in Step 2 persist under any simplicial functor by the union-composition construction of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]; Steps 3 and 4 already allow identities and degenerate acting edges. Thus repeated vertices or degenerate edges introduce no extra hypothesis. If $K$ has no vertices there are no triangles or precomposition instances, so the assertions are vacuous. No horn filler or mapping-space fibrancy has been used.

source.place: Section 1.1.5 functoriality of coherent realization; the same subset formulas for degenerate simplices.

lean.statement: theorem cone_triangle_mapping_square (C : CoherentNerveComparisonStatement.{u}) (K : SSet.{u}) : ∃ D : CanonicalEdges C K, (∀ {w x : K _⦋0⦌} (a : (hom (C.rigidification.obj K) (vertex C w) (vertex C x)) _⦋0⦌) (t : (value C x) _⦋1⦌), t ∈ (markedValue D x).marking → (precompose C a).app _ t ∈ (markedValue D w).marking) ∧ ∀ {x y z : K _⦋0⦌} (e : Edge x y) (f : Edge y z) (k : Edge x z) (σ : e.CompStruct f k), ∃ H : Δ[1] ⊗ Δ[1] ⟶ value C x, IsSquare D e f k σ H ∧ (action C x z).app _ ((D.coherenceEdge e f k σ).edge, (value C z).σ 0 (D.coneArrow z)) ∈ (markedValue D x).marking ∧ (k.edge ∈ Set.range (K.σ 0) → (D.coningEdge k).edge ∈ (markedValue D x).marking) ∧ ∀ (w : K _⦋0⦌) (a : (hom (C.rigidification.obj K) (vertex C w) (vertex C x)) _⦋0⦌), IsPrecomposedSquare D a e f k σ H
lean.note: Uses the recorded CoherentNerveComparisonStatement realization, ordered rightJoinCone, Mathlib subset-path nerves and Edge.CompStruct, and the recorded Marked type. CanonicalEdges fixes every named arrow and interval by equality with its complete coherent-simplex subset chain; the theorem states existence of those normalized data, all corners and full boundaries of each square, minimal marking membership and preservation under every vertex precomposition. No Kan or nondegeneracy assumption.
